summary.value: The White-faced Black Spanish is one of the oldest laying breeds in the West. It traces back to old Spanish stock but took its modern form in Britain and Holland in the 1700s, and the American Poultry Association accepted it in 1874. For most of the 1800s it was a leading egg bird in England and the eastern US. The plumage is a glossy green black, and a huge white face and earlobes hang down below the wattles. Roosters weigh about 8 pounds and hens about 6.5 pounds, and a bantam form exists. Hens seldom go broody and lay some 160 to 180 large chalk white eggs a year. The birds are active, noisy and curious, and a little aloof with other breeds. Years of breeding for bigger faces left them delicate, so they need shelter in both hot and cold weather and suit experienced keepers.
